summary:
Trend Detective is a map based web tool. This shows if the climate at any place on earth is really changing. We can either click on map to get the data or simply search by location name. The tool then pulls monthly data from NASA Power data that's built on MERRA-2, CERES and GPM IMERG and we are testing 12 measurement for the selected spot. Measurement like temperature, humidity, wind, sunlight and soil wetness.

How it actually work behind the scene is, it selects the variables, gets the data for a region for each variable, plots the time series, reports the rate of change per decade, and tests significance. We removed the seasonal cycle, averages by year, and uses the Mann-Kendall test with the Theil-Sen slope. Because 12 variables are tested at once, it corrects the p-values. Each result is marked "real change" or "could be random".

We also have a compare mode that puts two places side by side and flags opposite trends. Plain-language definitions help user learn to be data detectives and see the difference between a real trend and random variation.
details:
What it does

Trend Detective is a web app with a map. we click a place on the map or search for its name. The app gets monthly NASA POWER data for that place, from 1981 to 2025 (start year is selectable but currently limited to few years). It checks 12 things: air temperature, daytime high, nighttime low, ground temperature, rain, two kinds of humidity, wind, sunlight, two kinds of soil wetness, and air pressure.

How it works

It removes the seasons. Each month is compared with the normal for that month, so summer and winter do not hide the trend.

It makes one number for each year.

It finds how fast the value changes per decade.

It tests if the change is real or could be random, using the Mann-Kendall test. We test 12 things at once, so we make the test stricter to avoid lucky results.

A filled dot means "real change". A hollow dot means "could be random". The app also shows colored yearly stripes (blue is colder than average, red is warmer), a short sentence, a chart, and a simple explanation of each measurement.

Benefits and impact

User can test their own place and learn how to tell a real trend from luck. The app says "no clear trend" when there is not enough proof.

What is creative

One click checks all 12 things.

The dots make the result easy to read without knowing statistics.

Compare mode shows two places side by side. It marks a measurement only when it is real in both places and goes up in one and down in the other.

Tools

Python, Flask, NumPy, pandas, SciPy and matplotlib for the back end. Plain JavaScript, Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for the map. NASA POWER for the data. Open-Meteo and Nominatim for place names. pytest for tests.

What we thought about

NASA POWER data comes from models (MERRA-2, CERES, GPM IMERG). It is not a direct satellite reading. Each result is an average over an area about 50 km wide, not the exact spot you click.

We leave out 2026 because the year is not finished.

We skip soil wetness over open water.

We only test straight-line trends.

Some measurements are related, for example the three temperatures, so they are not separate findings.

Source code is public at: https://github.com/Rkymishra/climatrix/
